questions.question: What is a megacity, and how does a map show the sizes of major cities?
questions.expected_answer: A megacity is a city with more than ten million people in its wider urban area. On a world map of major cities, each city is shown with a circle or dot whose size shows the population, explained in the key. Many of the largest cities are in Asia, such as Tokyo, Delhi, Shanghai and Dhaka, and Africa has Cairo, Lagos and Kinshasa. Estimates vary because cities draw their borders differently.

questions.question: Describe the location of Cairo.
questions.expected_answer: Cairo is the capital of Egypt in north-eastern Africa. It lies on the banks of the River Nile, about one hundred and sixty kilometres south of the Mediterranean Sea, just south of where the narrow Nile valley opens into the wide, fertile delta. Egypt is almost all desert, and almost all its people live in the Nile valley and delta. Greater Cairo, including Giza, has more than twenty million people by many estimates.

questions.question: Explain four reasons why Cairo grew where it is.
questions.expected_answer: The Nile provides water for drinking, farming and industry in a desert country. The Nile's yearly floods left rich mud, making the soil fertile enough to grow food for many people. The river was a highway for boats, and Cairo's position where the valley meets the delta made it a meeting point for routes and trade between Africa, Asia and Europe, with the Suez Canal nearby. As a capital for more than a thousand years, it attracted rulers, scholars and traders and is now Egypt's centre of government, business and tourism.
